methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Project-Based Synthesis
content: Problem: Students learn grammar rules in isolation but struggle to combine them into a cohesive paragraph about themselves.

Solution: Week 14 acts as a capstone for Block A. There is no "new" grammar. Instead, students synthesize what they know to build a "Welcome to My World" poster. Session 1 focuses on drafting Identity & Family. Session 2 focuses on Abilities & Routines. Session 3 focuses on the final Presentation Delivery.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Bring students to the drafting table. Ask: "Who is in your family?" Student writes 1 sentence for their poster.
S2 pull-out: Ask: "What can you do?" and "What time do you wake up?". Student writes 2 sentences for their poster.
Communicative task: Information Gap (Section 8). Students practice asking presentation questions to their peers to prepare for the final Showcase.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  The Big Showcase Day
content: Today is the big day! Tom stands next to his poster.
He smiles at his teachers and friends.
"Welcome to my world!" Tom says loudly.
"I am Tom and I am a brave hero. This is my poster."
"I have a great family. We live in a modern city with tall buildings."
"I can run fast and I can ride a bike."
"Every morning, I wake up at seven o'clock. I eat a big breakfast."
"Then, I go to school to study Math."
Everyone claps. Tom's presentation is fantastic!
T / F: Tom stands next to a car.
T / F: Tom lives in a modern city.
Fill-in from text: "Then, I go to school to study _______________."
Stage 3B — Inference: Why does everyone clap for Tom?

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Luna's Poster: Abilities & Routines
content: Luna is making her poster for the Showcase.
"I want to write about my powers," she says.
She writes: "I can swim very fast in the water."
"I can jump high over the box!"
Luna draws a clock on her poster.
"Every day, I wake up early. I wake up at six o'clock."
"I go to school and I study hard."
She smiles at her beautiful poster.
"My daily routine is very busy. I am a great hero!"
T / F: Luna writes about her powers.
T / F: Luna wakes up late at night.
What does Luna draw on her poster?
Fill-in from text: "I go to school and I _______________ hard."

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W14: hero, family, happy, city, building
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (hero, family, happy, city, building) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Review: To be, Have, There is/are, Can, Present Simple
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Review: To be, Have, There is/are, Can, Present Simple.
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Community & Routines — Hero Showcase Day"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Community & Routines — Hero Showcase Day".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (hero, family, happy, city, building usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

teacher_contents.in_class_speaking:
IN-CLASS SPEAKING ACTIVITIES — Session 1 (teacher-led)

Activity 1 — Pair Speaking (3–5 min, pairs):
  Student A: Read your greeting ("Welcome to my world!").
  Student B: Introduce yourself ("I am [Name]. I have a big family.").

Challenge Extension (L3 — for advanced / older students):
  [O] L3 — Older: Fill in the blank with 3 options (10 items)
  Welcome _______________ (to / at / in) my world!
  I _______________ (am / is / are) a hero.
  I _______________ (have / has / can) a big family.
  I am very _______________ (happy / tall / fast) today.
